test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Parliamentary Committees of India is considered a ‘Financial Committee’?

options.text: Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs

solution:
The correct answer is __**Estimates Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Financial Committees:** In the Indian Parliament, there are three significant financial committees: **Public Accounts Committee**, **Estimates Committee**, and **Committee on Public Undertakings**. These committees play a crucial role in ensuring financial accountability and efficiency.
 
• **Estimates Committee:** The Estimates Committee is one of the key financial committees of the Parliament. It focuses on examining the estimates included in the budget presented to the Parliament.
 
• This committee evaluates whether the money allocated to various departments is being utilized efficiently and economically. It also suggests alternative policies to bring efficiency in financial administration. *Hence, the correct option is 'Estimates Committee'.*
 
• **Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs:** This committee is not a financial committee but focuses on ensuring the welfare of Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) by examining policies and programs related to their development and upliftment. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Committee on Petitions:** This committee examines petitions submitted to Parliament on various issues. It is not directly related to financial matters. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Committee on Privileges:** This committee ensures that the privileges of members of Parliament are upheld and examines cases of breach of privilege. It is not a financial committee. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Estimates Committee:**

 
 
• The Estimates Committee was constituted in **1950** under the provisions of the Constitution of India.
 
• It consists of **30 members**, all of whom are elected by the Lok Sabha from amongst its members. Members of the Rajya Sabha are not included.
 
• The term of office of the members is **one year**.
 
• Its main objective is to examine the budget estimates and suggest measures for improving the efficiency and economy of financial administration.
 
 
 
• **Public Accounts Committee:**
 
 
• This committee examines the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) and ensures accountability in government spending.
 
• It consists of **22 members** (15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha).
 
 
 
• **Committee on Public Undertakings:**
 
 
• This committee evaluates the performance of public sector enterprises and suggests measures for their improvement.
 
• It consists of **22 members** (15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha).
 
 
 
• **Non-Financial Committees:**
 
 
• Committees like the **Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs**, **Committee on Petitions**, and **Committee on Privileges** focus on social and administrative matters rather than financial issues.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Financial Committees:**

 
 
• These committees ensure **transparency** and **accountability** in the financial operations of the government.
 
• They provide recommendations for efficient utilization of public funds, thereby promoting economic growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Role of Estimates Committee:**
 
 
• The committee helps in identifying areas where resources are being wasted and suggests measures for improvement.
 
• It works to ensure that the budget allocation aligns with the priorities and goals of the government.
